feed.title: NPR Topics: News
feed.subtitle: Breaking news, top national and world stories, politics, business and culture from NPR. Catch up on demand with NPR News Now, Up First and Consider This.

entry.title: Virginia and D.C. sue to block construction of Trump arch
entry.summary: U.S. District Court Judge Tanya Chutkin ordered both sides to talk and to agree on a proposed briefing schedule on the motion for a temporary restraining order by Saturday evening.

entry.title: Mixed economic forecast weighs heavy ahead of midterms
entry.summary: There was a mixed Halloween bag of economic news this week. GDP growth is up, but so are prices. For now at least, interest rates are staying the same. What does that mean for the midterm elections?

entry.title: France seethes again as youth-led protests sweep Europe
entry.summary: French Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez warned of a "very high risk" of disorder, especially after dark on Halloween, as some 320,000 people nationwide took to the streets.

entry.title: Key takeaways from this week's political meeting in Beijing
entry.summary: The Communist party central committee meeting was focused on discipline and fighting corruption. It comes ahead of next year when Xi is widely expected to try to secure a fourth term.

entry.title: A simple explainer of the massive $6.3 billion crypto heist at Binance
entry.summary: Here are five things to know about the massive hack of the crypto exchange Binance — from how it happened to what it means for the sector.

entry.title: Justice Department seeks to isolate Alaska ballots amid criminal probe over Senate candidate
entry.summary: The latest developments come amid allegations, first reported by The New York Times, that Democrats recruited a spoiler candidate in the toss-up U.S. Senate race.

entry.title: Perspective: Forget the ballroom, we're headed to Cheesecake Factory!
entry.summary: Former President Obama caused a kerfuffle with his comments about President Trump's interior decorating at the White House. But maybe state dinners should happen at The Cheesecake Factory.

entry.title: Drone photo award winners: Far-out landscapes. Ship recycling. Rugs, rugs rugs!
entry.summary: The Siena Drone Photo Awards for 2026 offer breathtaking bird's-eye views of our planet, revealing landscapes, livelihoods and human stories often invisible from the ground.

entry.title: Do you have seasonal affective disorder? How to tell — and what to do about it
entry.summary: The syndrome can make people feel like a "hibernating bear," says Dr. Norman Rosenthal, who published the first research on SAD. He explains how to identify the symptoms and what to do to feel better.

entry.title: Can I trust the polls? And other questions from listeners about the 2026 midterms
entry.summary: Ahead of Election Day, listeners send in questions about whether debates are dead, if polls are reliable for election coverage and how Trump might work with Democrats if they win control of Congress.
